implementation.mode: Every adapter independently implements parsing, validation, error handling, business rules, and output assembly.
sharedArtifacts: expected exit status and error fragments

acceptance.mode: Each final bundle is executed as a subprocess against the same black-box cases.

authoring.mode: Weighted, evidence-backed review of the committed adapters against a shared 0-4 rubric.
authoring.interpretation: DX and maintainability are workload-specific authoring proxies. Every grade, weight, and evidence note is included in this report; they are not universal framework rankings.
authoring.scoreFormula: For each dimension, sum criterion weight × level / 4, then round to an integer from 0 to 100.

bundle.mode: func uses the minified CommonJS output from funcgo/Rolldown; competitors use minified, tree-shaken esbuild ESM targeting Node 24.
bundle.metric: Sum of the emitted level-9 gzip artifacts for all runtime JavaScript files. oclif uses explicit discovery with shared chunks.
bundle.exclusions: Build metadata and package manifests are excluded. oclif auto-transpilation is disabled and its optional development-only typescript loader is externalized.

source.mode: UTF-8 bytes and non-blank lines in each independent adapter implementation.
source.exclusions: Shared black-box fixtures, tests, build scripts, and report scripts.
source.interpretation: A context metric for implementation footprint, not a code-quality ranking.

runtime.mode: End-to-end wall time of a fresh Node.js process with piped stdout and stderr.
runtime.order: Framework order rotates for every sample to reduce ordering bias.

contract.requirement: Status plus project inspect/sync and audit list/export leaves, with unknown-command handling.
Profile, JSON, and trace options shared by every command from application scope.
Project and audit option sets each shared by multiple sibling commands without shared runtime benchmark code.
A root --context option replaces normal execution, with audit scope replacing its behavior.
Required, enum, aliased, defaulted, repeated, integer, boolean, and mutually exclusive options.
Audit export replaces the audit module format domain and default while retaining the module value.
Project conflicts use feature error policy while parser and other failures use application policy.
Deterministic text and JSON success output through one adapter-owned output boundary.

func-parser.applicationScope: shared parser option definition + explicit merge

dx.label: Type continuity
dx.measurement: How precisely shared option declarations flow into handlers without assertions, coercion, or duplicated interfaces.

dx.label: Scope composition
dx.measurement: How directly application and feature scopes share options and services across multiple commands.

dx.label: Validation authoring
dx.measurement: How much required, enum, repeated, numeric, and exclusive option behavior stays beside declarations.

dx.label: Alternate option actions
dx.measurement: How directly one option can replace normal command execution and be overridden in a nested scope.

dx.label: Boundary authoring
dx.measurement: How directly shared output plus application and feature error boundaries are expressed.

maintainability.label: Shared option locality
maintainability.measurement: Whether options shared by sibling commands have one explicit owner and one consumption path.

maintainability.label: Override locality
maintainability.measurement: Whether nested option and alternate-action overrides are declared where scope changes.

maintainability.label: Local glue burden
maintainability.measurement: How much parser-specific merging, normalization, dispatch, and interception remains.

maintainability.label: Command isolation
maintainability.measurement: Whether command behavior has explicit registration and ownership boundaries.

maintainability.label: Boundary locality
maintainability.measurement: Whether output and error policy are centralized at the intended application or feature scope.

alternate-actions.evidence: @OptionCommand replaces normal execution at application scope, and the audit module overrides it with overrideAll.

boundary-authoring.evidence: An injected @Stdout output service is shared through a module; module onError hooks define application and project failure policy.

scope-composition.evidence: AppOptions, ProjectOptions, AuditOptions, and Output are injected from their owning modules into sibling commands.

type-continuity.evidence: Decorator-backed class fields flow into handlers and services as typed instances without option-record assertions.

validation-authoring.evidence: @Required, @Enum, @ArrayString, @Value, @Flag, and @Exclusive keep the tested input policy on fields.

boundary-locality.evidence: Output is owned by OutputModule, project conflicts by ProjectModule, and remaining failures by AppModule.

command-isolation.evidence: Project handlers share one command class while audit leaves remain explicit commands registered by AuditModule.

local-glue.evidence: The adapter has no option-record merging or manual input normalization; output assembly and the project conflict remain local.

override-locality.evidence: @Override is attached to audit export format and the audit OptionCommand override is registered only in AuditModule.

shared-option-locality.evidence: Each shared option class is registered once at its owning module and injected into every consumer.

alternate-actions.evidence: Root and audit context behavior is implemented through explicit early interception in local dispatch code.

boundary-authoring.evidence: ParserError supplies structured parse failures, but output, application and feature classification, formatting, and exit status are all implemented locally.

scope-composition.evidence: Root, project, and audit parsers reuse one app option definition, with values merged explicitly across passthrough boundaries.

type-continuity.evidence: createParser infers command and option result unions, while AppInvocation and AppValues duplicate the shared application shape at the merge boundary.

validation-authoring.evidence: Primitive conversion and repeated values are declarative; defaults, required, enums, integers, and exclusivity remain local.

boundary-locality.evidence: One local catch owns failures, but project classification is not attached to a parser scope.

command-isolation.evidence: Root, project, and audit parsing have separate definitions; execution dispatch remains in one adapter flow.

local-glue.evidence: Nested routing requires passthrough parsing, application-option merging, dispatch, validation, and interception code.

override-locality.evidence: Audit format and context overrides are conditional values in local dispatch because parser definitions cannot override merged options.

shared-option-locality.evidence: Application options have one reusable definition, and project/audit options each have one feature parser owner.

alternate-actions.evidence: A shared helper checks --context from each action; audit callers explicitly choose the scoped context behavior.

boundary-authoring.evidence: One output helper and one final catch normalize behavior, while project classification is a local instanceof branch.

scope-composition.evidence: Reusable option factories model feature scope, but each action merges local and global option records.

type-continuity.evidence: Manual interfaces and assertions mirror option declarations at optsWithGlobals boundaries.

validation-authoring.evidence: choices, parsers, and conflicts are declarative; context-compatible required handling stays local.

boundary-locality.evidence: Output and final error normalization are centralized, but there is no feature-owned error boundary.

command-isolation.evidence: The command tree has explicit leaves, with registration and handlers retained in one adapter module.

local-glue.evidence: Each action merges global and local options and invokes local interception or required-option helpers.

override-locality.evidence: Audit export and audit context overrides are recreated through call-site arguments and replacement values.

shared-option-locality.evidence: Project and audit option factories remove declaration duplication but do not create an owned runtime scope.

alternate-actions.evidence: Handlers call context helpers before normal execution, with audit override behavior selected in the audit handler.

boundary-authoring.evidence: Shared output and fail helpers centralize policy; scoped project classification remains a local instanceof branch.

scope-composition.evidence: Command builders share feature options, while application options are global and feature state remains flat argv data.

type-continuity.evidence: Typed argument interfaces reach handlers, with declarations mirrored manually across builder and interface shapes.

validation-authoring.evidence: choices, number parsing, arrays, and conflicts are declarative; one audit check selects the action-specific enum.

boundary-locality.evidence: One final catch owns output, but feature error classification is not attached to a command scope.

command-isolation.evidence: Builders isolate project and audit declarations; action dispatch remains inside their shared handlers.

local-glue.evidence: Builder inference handles parsing while action dispatch, required handling, and interception remain local.

override-locality.evidence: Audit format and context differences are conditional values inside one audit builder and handler.

shared-option-locality.evidence: Project and audit builder functions provide one declaration path for their sibling actions.

alternate-actions.evidence: A base command supplies interception helpers, but every leaf must call one and export must replace context format manually.

boundary-authoring.evidence: Base-command output and one entry catch centralize behavior; project classification is local to the catch.

scope-composition.evidence: Shared flag objects and a base command compose application and feature behavior across independent commands.

type-continuity.evidence: Flags infer leaf command values, and shared helpers consume explicit AppFlags and AuditFlags contracts.

validation-authoring.evidence: options, integer parsing, repeated flags, and exclusivity remain declarative in shared flag definitions.

boundary-locality.evidence: Output lives on the base command and all failures converge at the entry point, without feature-owned registration.

command-isolation.evidence: Every leaf is an independent Command class registered in the explicit discovery map.

local-glue.evidence: Parsing needs little normalization, while context interception is repeated once in every run method.

override-locality.evidence: Export owns a distinct flag definition, but scoped context replacement is assembled in the run method.

shared-option-locality.evidence: Application, project, and audit flag objects are reusable, explicit declaration owners.

alternate-actions.evidence: Handlers explicitly invoke local interception helpers and select the audit replacement values.

boundary-authoring.evidence: Local helpers own output, catching, classification, and exit status without scoped framework boundaries.

scope-composition.evidence: Global options are shared, while project and audit declarations and normalization remain on flat command schemas.

type-continuity.evidence: Handlers receive broad option records and narrow or convert their values locally.

validation-authoring.evidence: Defaults are declared, while enum, required, integer, repeated, and exclusivity behavior is implemented locally.

boundary-locality.evidence: One local catch centralizes failures, but project scope is only an instanceof branch.

command-isolation.evidence: Command schemas create named sections, while action dispatch and all normalization remain in their handlers.

local-glue.evidence: Broad option records require local enum, integer, list, required, conflict, and interception helpers.

scale.label: absent
scale.meaning: The tested workflow has no practical support for this criterion.

scale.label: local
scale.meaning: The adapter implements the concern locally with little framework help.

scale.label: mixed
scale.meaning: Framework primitives help, but recurring local glue is still required.

scale.label: supported
scale.meaning: The framework carries the concern with small integration code.

scale.label: direct
scale.meaning: A typed framework mechanism carries the concern without duplicate rules.
